title: Strict henselization under a quasi-finite local map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map, let $p\subset A$ and $q\subset B$ be primes with $q$ lying over $p$, and assume $A\to B$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] (in particular this applies when $A\to B$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]). Choose an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and compatible geometric point maps $\kappa(p)\to\Omega$ and $\kappa(q)\to\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the strict henselizations formed from the pointed etale-neighbourhood colimits with the induced separable closures in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Then the canonical map $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\to B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a finite local homomorphism. Its residue-field extension is finite purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Moreover $B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is canonically the localization of $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A_p}B_q$ at the prime ideal which is the kernel of the induced map $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A_p}B_q\to\Omega$.
